identity.title: [v0.92][C-SDLC][defect] Recover initialized decomposed issue cards without rewriting history

values.task_boundary: Implement only the csdlc-edit tooling route, tests, and docs needed for initialized post-decomposition card recovery using #114 gen35 as a read-only golden fixture.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A typed initialized recovery request can transform a stale decomposed-parent packet to coordination-only truth without binding, branch mutation, GitHub writes, publication, merge, closeout, product-code changes, bootstrap overwrite, or #114 mutation.

AC-2: Recovery preserves append-only audit history, generation/digest CAS, branch/worktree null state, every existing design/diagram byte, and records exact old/new design-review authority truth when clearing or replacing a false approval such as operator:planning-1-assignment.

AC-3: Recovery validates all requested semantic replacements before writing, stages post-state bytes as content-addressed blobs under an issue-local write-ahead journal, fsyncs blobs/manifest/directories where supported, writes a prepared manifest as the durable point of no return, writes a commit marker only after postimage verification, abandons transactions without a durable prepared manifest, rolls forward any prepared transaction to the exact post-state, and fails closed on unexpected target hashes.

AC-4: Recovery enforces canonical request-root/cwd identity, repository containment, issue/path identity, symlink and escape rejection, and copies the #114 fixture to an isolated golden root before any mutation test.
AC-5: Recovery records SOR preparation truth without claiming execution, implementation, publication, merge, closeout, or terminal authority.
AC-6: Recovery updates or explicitly dispositions title/slug/version identity consistently across every card projection without changing issue number or repository.
AC-7: Recovery distinguishes historical gen0 design evidence from current implementation authority and rejects bootstrap regeneration as a way to overwrite preserved evidence.

AC-8: Recovery accepts a generic typed graph of node IDs, roles, directed dependency edges, parent integration owner, and in-scope status; it validates acyclicity/order and fails closed on missing/inverted edges, out-of-scope nodes, duplicate roles, or cross-child trust redefinition.

AC-9: Recovered packets can pass doctor/validate after valid #119 design/card review is recorded, without requiring bind or product proof, and normal initialized edits remain rejected except through the explicit recovery route.

AC-10: Failure output is typed JSON with exact rejected reasons for stale digest, missing preserved evidence, unsafe scope, unsupported phase, graph mismatch, request-root/cwd mismatch, path escape, symlink, unsupported fsync/durability fallback, non-atomic journal/manifest/commit-marker staging failure, unexpected target hash, or attempted #114/root-lock mutation.
non_goals: Mutating root lock state or #112 worktrees
Creating, updating, closing, or retitling other issues
Publishing, merging, closeout, AWS, #84, #122, #203, or #256 work
